plan.planning_summary: This control axis tests thickness optimization on a fixed 24-layer HfO2/SiO2 dichroic stack for dual-band spectral control. The hypothesis is that gradient-based thickness tuning on a high-layer-count alternating stack can simultaneously achieve high transmittance at 1530-1565 nm and high reflectance at 400-700 nm. This route uses only the model's prior knowledge of quarter-wave stack physics and dichroic filter design patterns, with no literature retrieval. The refinement narrows the search window by reducing perturbation amplitude and targeting specific thick layers that dominate optical path length.

routes.title: 24-layer HfO2/SiO2 dichroic stack with refined thickness optimization
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A 24-layer alternating HfO2/SiO2 stack with individually optimized thicknesses can achieve simultaneous high transmittance in 1530-1565 nm and high reflectance in 400-700 nm, with the thickest layers (layers 3 and 6) being primary drivers for spectral alignment.
routes.design_principle: Dichroic filters work by creating constructive interference in reflection for the stopband and destructive interference for the passband. Higher layer counts provide more degrees of freedom for dual-band optimization. Thicker layers contribute more optical path length and thus have greater leverage on the spectral position of interference features.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | Fused Silica substrate (24 layers total, alternating starting with HfO2)
design_variables: Individual layer thicknesses for all 24 layers
Perturbation initialization amplitude (reduced from 5 nm to 2 nm)
Targeted local refinement on layers 3 and 6
soft_objectives: Maximize average transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band
Maximize average reflectance in 400-700 nm band
Maintain physically valid candidates (no negative thickness, no absorption violations)
manufacturing_considerations: Total layer count fixed at 24 (within 30-layer limit)
All thicknesses must be positive and manufacturable (typically >20 nm)
HfO2 and SiO2 are standard evaporated/sputtered coating materials
theory_basis: Recalled knowledge: Quarter-wave stacks centered at a wavelength produce high reflectance at that wavelength; dichroic designs require non-quarter-wave thicknesses to create dual-band behavior
Recalled knowledge: HfO2 has higher refractive index (~2.0 at 1550 nm) than SiO2 (~1.45 at 1550 nm), providing good index contrast for interference
Recalled knowledge: More layers provide more optimization degrees of freedom but increase manufacturing complexity and stress
Recalled knowledge: Thicker layers have greater optical path length contribution and thus stronger influence on spectral feature positioning
expected_advantages: 24 layers provide sufficient degrees of freedom for dual-band optimization
Alternating high/low index structure is a standard, manufacturable design pattern
Reduced perturbation amplitude (2 nm vs 5 nm) should produce more stable convergence near local optima
Targeted refinement on layers 3 and 6 addresses the identified primary drivers of spectral mismatch
known_risks: Uncertainty: Exact refractive index dispersion of HfO2 and SiO2 across 400-1565 nm range - the material catalog datasets will resolve this, but my recollection of specific n values is approximate
Uncertainty: Whether 24 layers is optimal vs 26 or 28 layers within the 30-layer limit - this route fixes 24 to maintain a single axis
Uncertainty: Whether the alternating HfO2-first sequence is optimal vs SiO2-first - this route fixes the sequence to isolate thickness as the only variable
Risk: Local optimization may converge to a local rather than global optimum; the reduced perturbation amplitude may limit escape from local minima
Risk: Layers 3 and 6 refinement assumption may be incorrect - other layer combinations might be more influential
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 24-layer planar multilayer dielectric stack under frequency-domain plane-wave illumination. Stack topology: Air incident medium, then 24 alternating layers starting with HfO2, then SiO2 (Lemarchand), repeating (HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand), HfO2, SiO2 (Lemarchand)), terminated by Fused Silica substrate. Design variables: all 24 individual layer thicknesses in nanometers. Optimization uses gradient-based thickness tuning with perturbation initialization amplitude of 2 nm (reduced from 5 nm). Apply targeted local refinement pass on layer 3 (index 2, 0-based) and layer 6 (index 5, 0-based) due to their larger optical path length contribution. Wavelength bands: maximize transmittance in 1530-1565 nm, maximize reflectance in 400-700 nm. Incidence angle: normal incidence (0 degrees) as default since not specified. Polarization: unpolarized or both TE and TM averaged. Manufacturing constraint: total layer count is exactly 24 (within 30-layer limit). Materials: hfo2 and SiO2 (Lemarchand) only, resolved from material catalog. Performance targets are soft ranking preferences, not pass/fail gates.
routes.revision_reason: Continuation of control route with refined optimization parameters: reduced thickness perturbation initialization amplitude from 5 nm to 2 nm for narrower search window, and targeted local refinement on layers 3 and 6 (0-based indices 2 and 5) identified as primary drivers for spectral mismatch resolution based on their larger physical thicknesses and higher accumulated optical path length.

plan.knowledge_source_disclosure: This route was planned from the model's own prior knowledge alone. No Semantic Scholar query was issued, no retrieved paper reached the prompt, and no method-research report was supplied -- neither for the initial plan nor for any continuation round. It is the control arm of a controlled comparison against the literature-grounded routes, and its evidence-id allowlist is empty by construction.
unresolved_decisions: Whether 24 layers is the optimal count within the 30-layer limit, or if 26 or 28 would perform better - this route fixes 24 to maintain a single optimization axis
Whether HfO2-first alternating sequence is optimal vs SiO2-first - fixed to isolate thickness as the variable
Exact refractive index values for HfO2 and SiO2 across the full 400-1565 nm spectrum - resolved by material catalog datasets at execution
Optimal incidence angle if not normal incidence - this route assumes 0 degrees as default since user did not specify
plan.stop_if_all_routes_fail: If this control route cannot achieve best_target_score above 0.85 after 5 rounds with the refined parameters, the fundamental hypothesis about 24-layer alternating HfO2/SiO2 stacks for this dual-band requirement may need revision - either layer count, material pair, or topology sequence would need to change, which would constitute a new route axis.

expected_observations: best_target_score should rise or remain stable across rounds as the narrower perturbation window refines near optima
valid_candidates count should remain high (>=5) since thickness constraints are not tightened
tightest_margin should not fall significantly across rounds if the refinement is converging properly
thicknesses_nm for layers 3 and 6 should show smaller variation between rounds compared to other layers as targeted refinement stabilizes them
If the hypothesis is wrong, best_target_score may plateau early or valid_candidates may drop if the 2 nm perturbation is too restrictive
stop_conditions: if best_target_score improves by less than 1e-3 against the historical best for two consecutive rounds, treat the axis as exhausted, stop and keep the current best
if valid_candidates falls below 3 for two consecutive rounds, relax the perturbation amplitude back to 5 nm and continue
if tightest_margin falls below 0.1 for two consecutive rounds, reduce the refinement weight on layers 3 and 6 and redistribute optimization effort across all layers

selector_prompt.system:
You are the internal material-dataset selector inside a scientific TMM
harness. This is not route planning and you must not redesign the route.
Return exactly one JSON object and no markdown:
{"selections":[{"request_id":"material_01","selected_rank":1,"provider":"rii_sqlite","dataset_id":562,"reason":"..."}]}

The user question is authoritative. Each request contains candidates already
retrieved from the local MaterialRegistry and sorted by three equal physical
metrics: target-band coverage, n/k completeness, and sampling density. Rank 1
is the most physically reliable candidate; lower rank means less reliable.
Choose exactly one candidate from the supplied list for every request. Never
invent, rename, or edit a provider or dataset_id. The selected_rank must point
to the selected array element, and provider/dataset_id must copy that element.

Material identity, stoichiometry, explicit material state/preparation, and an
explicit requested source are hard constraints. A candidate with
formula_exact=false or semantic_match=same_element_family is not an allowed
substitute for a formula request. SiO is not SiO2, even if the SiO2 candidate
has better physical coverage. When several candidates satisfy the hard
constraints, select the highest-ranked one (usually rank 1). If no candidate
satisfies them, return selected_rank:null, provider:null, dataset_id:null and
reason:"needs_confirmation" for that request.
